title: Production Administrator
description:
Job Description:

The Production Administrator is responsible for collecting, recording, validating, and reporting production data across the companies manufacturing operations. The role focuses on monitoring yields, waste, production outputs, and key operational metrics, ensuring that factory performance information is accurate, timely, and reliable.

The position will conduct routine audits of production records, analyse performance data, and provide management with clear reporting to support operational decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Monitoring, Data collection & Reporting
- Record and monitor production yields across all manufacturing departments.
- Track yield performance against established standards and targets.
- Investigate and document yield variances.
- Maintain accurate yield records and reporting systems.
- Gather production data from manufacturing operations.
- Record production outputs, waste levels, downtime, and throughput information.
- Produce daily, weekly, and monthly performance reports.
- Generate KPI reports and trend analysis for management.
- Ensure all reporting is accurate, timely, and consistent.

Auditing & Verification
- Conduct routine audits of production records and data collection processes.
- Verify the accuracy and completeness of production paperwork and system entries.
- Identify discrepancies and work with operational teams to resolve them.
- Support internal and external audits by providing accurate production information.

Performance Analysis
- Analyse production data to identify trends, variances, and opportunities for improved reporting accuracy.
- Monitor key factory metrics including:
- Yield
- Waste
- Production Output
- Downtime
- Material Usage
- Prepare summaries and reports for management review.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Experience working in a food manufacturing or production environment.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office.
- Ability to collect, organise, and interpret production data.
- Strong communication and organisational skills.

Desirable Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in production reporting, yield analysis, or factory administration.
- Experience using ERP or production management systems.
- Knowledge of manufacturing KPIs and production performance measures.

Personal Attributes

Methodical and highly organised.

Detail-focused with a commitment to data accuracy.

Confident working on the factory floor and within an office environment.

Able to work independently and manage multiple reporting deadlines.

Work Location: In person

description: Join our friendly and supportive GP practice as a Medical Receptionist, where youll play a vital role in helping patients access the right care and supporting the smooth running of our busy primary care team. Were looking for someone who is approachable, organised and compassionate, with excellent communication skills and a genuine desire to help people. Youll be part of a welcoming team where no two days are the same, working closely with GPs, nurses and other healthcare professionals. If you enjoy working with people, thrive in a busy environment and want a rewarding role where you can make a real difference to patients and your local community, wed love to hear from you. The Medical Receptionist will be a key point of contact for our patients, providing a friendly, professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. You will help patients access the most appropriate care, manage appointment requests and support a wide range of day-to-day administrative tasks. The role involves working closely with GPs, nurses and the wider practice team, handling patient enquiries sensitively and confidentially, processing information accurately and helping to ensure the practice runs smoothly. You will need to be organised, adaptable and confident working in a busy environment while always providing excellent patient care. Working hours 26 hours per week: Monday: 8:30am 4:40pm Tuesday: 8:30am 2:00pm Wednesday: 8:30am 4:30pm Thursday: 8:30am 2:00pm Friday: Non-working day Please note that although Friday is your usual non-working day, flexibility is essential, and you will be required to work Fridays when necessary to provide annual leave cover for other members of the reception team. Job Description Medical Receptionist Job Title: Medical Receptionist Hours: 26 hours per week Responsible to: Practice Manager / Deputy Practice Manager To provide a professional, efficient and welcoming reception service to patients and support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The Medical Receptionist is often the first point of contact for our patients and therefore plays an important role in their experience of the practice. The successful candidate will need to communicate with compassion and professionalism while maintaining confidentiality and dealing effectively with a busy and varied workload. Answer incoming telephone calls and deal with patient enquiries appropriately. Use care navigation skills to help patients access the most appropriate member of the healthcare team or service. Book, amend and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Process requests and enquiries from patients, clinicians and other healthcare professionals. Accurately record and update patient information on the clinical system. Assist patients with general queries and explain practice procedures and available services. Manage incoming correspondence, tasks and electronic communications and direct these to the appropriate person or team. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community services and other healthcare providers when required. Assist with administrative duties including scanning, filing, document processing and other general office tasks. Maintain patient confidentiality at all times and comply with information governance and data protection requirements. Recognise potentially urgent situations and escalate concerns appropriately in accordance with practice procedures. Deal with challenging or sensitive situations calmly, professionally and compassionately. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare professionals, reception colleagues and the wider practice team. Attend team meetings, training sessions and protected learning events as required. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role to support the effective running of the practice. The contracted hours for this position are 26 hours per week , worked as follows: Monday: 8:30am 4:40pm Tuesday: 8:30am 2:00pm Wednesday: 8:30am 4:30pm Thursday: 8:30am 2:00pm Friday: Usual non-working day Flexibility is an important requirement of this position. Although Friday will normally be your non-working day, you will be required to work on Fridays when necessary to provide annual leave cover for other members of the reception team. The post holder will have access to confidential information relating to patients, their families, practice staff and other healthcare professionals. All information must be treated in the strictest confidence and handled in accordance with practice policies, UK GDPR and relevant legislation. All employees have a responsibility to take reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of colleagues, patients and visitors. The post holder will be expected to follow practice health and safety procedures and report any concerns appropriately. The practice is committed to providing an inclusive environment for patients and staff. The post holder must treat everyone with dignity and respect and support the practice's commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. The successful candidate will receive appropriate induction and training and will be expected to participate in ongoing training and development relevant to their role. Previous experience within a GP practice or NHS environment would be advantageous; however, we also welcome applications from candidates with strong customer service, reception or administrative experience who have the right attitude and are willing to learn. This job description is intended as a guide to the main responsibilities of the role and may be amended from time to time to reflect the changing needs of the practice and primary care.
